Early-Exit and Instant Confidence Translation Quality Estimation
Vilém Zouhar, Maike Züfle, Beni Egressy, Julius Cheng, Mrinmaya Sachan, Jan Niehues

path.aria-label: Predict quality and confidence at each layer
Decide when to exit for faster evaluation

g.aria-label: src: "Ich glaube ich spinne." tgt: "I believe I spider."
make metric predict human quality assessment
make metric also predict absolute distance from human quality assessment

Automatic metrics for machine translation are usually trained to predict how good translation is given the source (and possibly a reference). We make them predict their confidence in this assessment as well:
Alternative is Monte Carlo dropout, which runs the metric multiple times. Instant confidence runs once.
At each layer in the metric we get estimate of translation quality and the current confidence:
We can stop computation at any layer if confidence is high enough or predictions do not change much anymore (variance):

path.aria-label: This prevents unnecessary computation. Real examples of early-exit:

g.aria-label:
Producing 1000 hypotheses is easy e.g. parallel sampling or beam search). Determining which one is the best one is the hard part.
- Running COMET on all hypotheses is too expensive. - Treat each hypothesis as an "arm" (multi-armed bandit). Pulling it computes the next Early-Exit COMET layer. This costs a little but gives a more accurate quality estimate.
